name: Particle Morph
description: Thousands of particles flow between shapes — sphere, torus, DNA helix, cube, wave — each easing at its own rate so the morph ripples instead of snapping.
a11y: Canvas is decorative (keep meaningful copy in HTML). Under reduced motion the shell switches to an on-demand frameloop and renders one still frame.
perf: One Points draw call; positions updated on the CPU (8k particles ≈ 0.3 ms). Lower `count` on mobile.
prompt: Build a React Three Fiber particle morph. Precompute Float32Array target positions for each shape (Fibonacci sphere, torus, double helix, cube surface, wave grid) with the same particle count. In useFrame, move every particle toward the current target with a per-index rate (k = dt·(1.6 + (i%97)/40)) so the morph ripples, flag the position attribute for update, rotate slowly and tilt toward the pointer. Advance the target every `hold` seconds. Additive blending, vertex colours lerped across two colours. Render inside a canvas shell that pauses off-screen and renders a still frame under reduced motion.

name: Sphere Gallery
description: Photos tiled over a sphere (Fibonacci lattice, each tile facing outward) that you grab and spin with inertia, settling back into a slow idle rotation.
a11y: Canvas is decorative — also provide the images as an HTML list or link grid. Drag uses pointer events (touch works, vertical page scroll preserved). Reduced motion: no idle spin.
perf: 48 textured planes, textures shared via useTexture; fog hides the back so overdraw is low.
prompt: Build a draggable 3D sphere gallery in React Three Fiber. Place N planes on a Fibonacci sphere; orient each with Matrix4.lookAt so its front faces outward. Load images with drei useTexture (sRGB). Listen to pointerdown/move/up on the canvas element: while dragging, set angular velocity from the pointer delta; when released, ease velocity back to an idle spin. Clamp the X tilt. Add fog so far tiles fade. Under reduced motion drop the idle spin.

name: Glass Shape
description: A refracting glass object (drei MeshTransmissionMaterial) floating in front of coloured shapes — real refraction, chromatic dispersion, faceted or smooth cut — tilting toward the pointer.
a11y: Canvas is decorative (keep meaningful copy in HTML). Under reduced motion the shell switches to an on-demand frameloop and renders one still frame. Temporal distortion is turned off.
perf: Transmission renders the scene twice; DPR capped at 1.75 and resolution 512. Use one glass object per page.
prompt: Build a glass hero object with React Three Fiber + drei MeshTransmissionMaterial (thickness 1.4, ior 1.35, chromaticAberration, backside, samples 6). Put bright coloured primitives behind it so refraction is visible, wrap it in drei Float, rotate slowly and ease rotation toward the pointer. Offer faceted (flatShading, low detail) vs smooth. Light it with drei Environment + Lightformers (no HDR download). Cap DPR at 1.75.

name: Shader Blob
description: A living sphere — simplex-noise vertex displacement and a fresnel rim in a custom ShaderMaterial. Hover makes the surface boil; colours blend by noise height.
a11y: Canvas is decorative (keep meaningful copy in HTML). Under reduced motion the shell switches to an on-demand frameloop and renders one still frame.
perf: All deformation on the GPU (icosahedron detail 64); one draw call.
prompt: Build a shader blob in React Three Fiber: icosahedronGeometry(1.35, 64) with a ShaderMaterial. Vertex: 3D simplex noise of normal*1.6 + time, displace along the normal by uAmp, pass noise, view-space normal and view vector. Fragment: mix two colours by smoothstep(noise), add a fresnel rim (pow(1−dot(n,v),2.2)) mixed toward a third colour. On pointer over, ease uAmp up by 2.4×. Under reduced motion freeze time.

name: Spiral Galaxy
description: A procedural spiral galaxy: tens of thousands of particles thrown along winding arms, warm core fading to a cool rim, with pointer-driven camera drift.
a11y: Canvas is decorative (keep meaningful copy in HTML). Under reduced motion the shell switches to an on-demand frameloop and renders one still frame.
perf: 40k points in one draw call, generated once in useMemo.
prompt: Generate a spiral galaxy with three.js Points: for each particle pick radius r = random^1.6·R, branch angle = (i % branches)/branches·2π, twist = r·spin; offset by random^3 noise (sign random) that grows with r; colour lerps inside→outside by r/R. Additive blending, no depth write. Rotate slowly and drift the camera toward the pointer while it keeps looking at the origin.

name: Orbit Sphere
description: A dotted planet with tilted orbit rings and satellites — the classic "global network / coverage" hero visual.
a11y: Canvas is decorative (keep meaningful copy in HTML). Under reduced motion the shell switches to an on-demand frameloop and renders one still frame.
perf: ~2.4k points plus a few dozen tiny spheres; ring groups rotate as wholes.
prompt: Build an orbit sphere hero in React Three Fiber: a Fibonacci-sphere Points cloud over a dark occluding sphere, plus several tilted ring groups (thin torus + N small spheres on the circle, first one larger in an accent colour). Rotate each ring group around its own axis at alternating speeds, spin the whole rig slowly and ease its X tilt toward the pointer.

name: Wave Terrain
description: A rolling field of points displaced on the GPU, with a ripple that follows the cursor across the ground plane — press to amplify. Depth fog dissolves the horizon.
a11y: Canvas is decorative (keep meaningful copy in HTML). Under reduced motion the shell switches to an on-demand frameloop and renders one still frame.
perf: ~20k points, all motion in the vertex shader; the pointer is raycast onto a math plane (no mesh raycasting).
prompt: Build a GPU wave terrain: a grid of points (resolution²) at y=0 rendered with a ShaderMaterial. Vertex shader sums a few sin/cos waves of x, z and time, adds a ripple exp(−d²·.35)·sin(3d − 4t) around uPointer, sets gl_PointSize by depth. Fragment discards outside a circle and fogs by depth. Each frame raycast the pointer onto Plane(y=0) and lerp uPointer to the hit; pointerdown raises uPress.

name: Image Ribbon
description: Photos wrapped on a tilted, genuinely curved ribbon (open cylinder slices) that drifts and spins faster with wheel or drag.
a11y: Canvas is decorative — mirror the projects as HTML links. Wheel listener is passive so page scroll still works. Reduced motion: no drift.
perf: One cylinder slice per image; textures shared.
prompt: Build a curved image ribbon in React Three Fiber: for each image create an open CylinderGeometry slice (thetaStart = i·(arc+gap), thetaLength = arc) textured with that image, inside a group tilted on Z. Add wheel + drag velocity that decays back to an idle drift; ease the tilt with the pointer. Dispose geometries on unmount.

name: 3D Coin Flip
description: A metallic coin with canvas-drawn embossed faces. It flips on a spring with a little hop and tilts toward the pointer — fintech/rewards hero.
a11y: Decorative; announce results in HTML (demo uses aria-live). Reduced motion: flips snap to the final face.
perf: CanvasTexture faces generated once; one cylinder with three material groups.
prompt: Build a 3D coin: cylinderGeometry(1.25, 1.25, .16, 96) rotated so its cap faces the camera, with three materials (edge metal, front and back faces using CanvasTextures drawn with a radial gradient, rim ring, ridges and a label). Flip: add 3π to a target and integrate a damped spring toward it each frame plus a sin-curve hop. Tilt with the pointer. Light with drei Environment Lightformers.

name: Warp Tunnel
description: An endless tunnel of glowing polygon rings (one InstancedMesh) streaming toward the camera; the far end bends toward the pointer.
a11y: Canvas is decorative (keep meaningful copy in HTML). Under reduced motion the shell switches to an on-demand frameloop and renders one still frame.
perf: 80 instances in one draw call; matrices + colours updated per frame.
prompt: Build a warp tunnel with a three.js InstancedMesh of thin tori (low radial segments make polygons). Each frame advance z modulo the spacing, position ring i at z = −i·spacing + offset, bend its x/y by steer·(depth fraction)² where steer lerps toward the pointer, spin slowly, and set an instance colour that brightens as rings approach. Black fog.

name: Instanced Pillar Grid
description: A field of 1,296 pillars (one InstancedMesh) that rise and glow under the cursor and breathe gently at rest.
a11y: Canvas is decorative (keep meaningful copy in HTML). Under reduced motion the shell switches to an on-demand frameloop and renders one still frame.
perf: One draw call; per-frame matrix updates for ~1.3k instances. The pointer is raycast onto a plane.
prompt: Build an instanced pillar grid: InstancedMesh of unit boxes, size² instances. Each frame raycast the pointer onto the y=0 plane, compute each pillar's distance d (in cells), lift = max(0, 1 − d/radius), target height = .15 + idle waves + lift²·1.6, ease heights toward targets, write matrices (scale y = height, y = height/2) and lerp instance colour toward the accent by lift. Camera at an isometric-ish angle looking at the origin.

name: Floating Shapes
description: Playful clay-like primitives bobbing in a soft studio — pointer parallax, hover swell, contact shadows.
a11y: Canvas is decorative (keep meaningful copy in HTML). Under reduced motion the shell switches to an on-demand frameloop and renders one still frame.
perf: 14 meshes with physical materials; ContactShadows rendered once per frame at low res.
prompt: Build a playful 3D hero: ~14 primitives (sphere, torus, capsule, box, cone, knot) placed on a golden-angle spiral, each wrapped in drei Float with clearcoat physical materials from a candy palette. Hovering a shape eases its scale up 18%. A Rig group eases its rotation toward the pointer. drei ContactShadows under the scene, Environment Lightformers for soft light.

name: Scroll Camera Waypoints
description: A scroll-driven camera flight: a ScrollTrigger-scrubbed GSAP timeline tweens a plain object between waypoints and the R3F camera copies it each frame; captions crossfade per stop.
inspiration: GSAP Demo Hub — three.js scroll waypoints
a11y: Captions are real HTML. Reduced motion: no camera flight — every waypoint becomes a static card.
perf: Sticky canvas + scrub:1; the camera is only written in useFrame, GSAP never touches three.js objects directly.
prompt: Build a scroll-driven three.js camera tour: a tall section with a sticky R3F Canvas. Keep a plain rig object {px,py,pz,tx,ty,tz}; a GSAP timeline with a scrub:1 ScrollTrigger tweens it from waypoint to waypoint (one unit each) and crossfades HTML captions. A CameraRig component copies rig → camera.position and lookAt in useFrame. Reduced motion: render the waypoints as static cards.
